_comment: Every function an expression can call, as the editor offers it: the function
picker, the function library and the help all read this file.
It is a claim about the engine, and pkg/infra/evaluator/function_catalog_test.go
holds it to that: the names must be exactly the ones CallFunction runs, and
each `example`, evaluated against `source`, must answer `result`. Add a
function to the engine and that test fails until it is listed here.
`args` are the placeholders the picker inserts -- name(args...) -- and
`volatile` marks an example with no fixed answer, which is shown without one.
`keywords` are other words someone might search for it by.

functions.name: lower
functions.summary: Text in lowercase.

functions.name: upper
functions.summary: Text in uppercase.

functions.name: trim
functions.summary: Text without the spaces, tabs and line breaks at either end.

functions.name: concat
functions.summary: Joins any number of values into one text. A missing value adds nothing.

functions.name: replace
functions.summary: Replaces every occurrence of find. Upper and lower case are different letters.

functions.name: substring
functions.summary: Part of a text, from position start (the first character is 0) up to but not including end, or to the end of the text. Positions count bytes, so an accented letter or an emoji takes more than one.

functions.name: split
functions.summary: Cuts a text at each separator and trims the parts. Without index the result is the list of parts; with one it is that part, counted from 0, or from the end when negative.

functions.name: len
functions.summary: How many characters the text has -- characters, not bytes, so é is one. For a list, how many items; for an object, how many keys.

functions.name: starts_with
functions.summary: true when the text begins with prefix. Upper and lower case are different letters.

functions.name: ends_with
functions.summary: true when the text ends with suffix. Upper and lower case are different letters.

functions.name: pad_left
functions.summary: Widens the text to width characters by adding pad -- a space unless given -- in front. Text already that wide is left whole. width is a whole number up to 10000.

functions.name: pad_right
functions.summary: Widens the text to width characters by adding pad -- a space unless given -- after it. Text already that wide is left whole. width is a whole number up to 10000.

functions.name: regex_extract
functions.summary: The first part of the text the regular expression matches, or one group of it by number or by name. null when nothing matches. Patterns use Go's RE2 syntax, up to 1024 characters.

functions.name: regex_replace
functions.summary: Replaces every part the regular expression matches. In with, $1 or ${name} stands for a group. null when the pattern is not valid.

functions.name: title
functions.summary: Every word starting with a capital and the rest in lowercase.

functions.name: slug
functions.summary: Text made safe for a URL: lowercase letters and digits, accents dropped, everything else one hyphen.

functions.name: normalize_space
functions.summary: Text with every run of spaces, tabs and line breaks made one space, and none at either end.

functions.name: add
functions.summary: a + b. Text holding a number is read as that number; anything else counts as 0.

functions.name: sub
functions.summary: a - b.

functions.name: mul
functions.summary: a × b.

functions.name: div
functions.summary: a ÷ b. Dividing by zero gives null rather than an error.

functions.name: round
functions.summary: Rounds to the nearest whole number, or to the given number of decimals.

functions.name: abs
functions.summary: A number without its sign.

functions.name: floor
functions.summary: The number rounded down to a whole number.

functions.name: ceil
functions.summary: The number rounded up to a whole number.

functions.name: mod
functions.summary: The remainder of a divided by b, with the sign of a. null when b is 0.

functions.name: pow
functions.summary: base raised to the power of exponent. null when there is no finite answer.

functions.name: min
functions.summary: The smallest of the numbers, including the items of a list. Values that are not numbers are skipped.

functions.name: max
functions.summary: The largest of the numbers, including the items of a list. Values that are not numbers are skipped.

functions.name: clamp
functions.summary: The number kept between low and high: below low it is low, above high it is high.

functions.name: format_number
functions.summary: The number as text with a thousands separator and decimals places, rounded as round() rounds. locale is en (1,234.50), de, id, it or nl (1.234,50) or fr (1 234,50).

functions.name: now
functions.summary: The time the record is processed, as text like 2024-03-09T14:30:00+07:00, in the server's time zone.

functions.name: timestamp
functions.summary: The time the record is processed, as a number: seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC.

functions.name: date_format
functions.summary: Rewrites a date in another layout. A layout shows how the reference date 2 Jan 2006 15:04:05 would be written: "2006-01-02", or "02 Jan 2006 15:04". from_layout says how to read a date that is not ISO or year-month-day. A date that cannot be read is left as it was.

functions.name: toDate
functions.summary: Reads a date and writes it as an ISO timestamp. layout says how the text is written, in the same reference-date form date_format uses. Text that cannot be read gives null.

functions.name: date_add
functions.summary: The date moved by a duration: 90m, 1h30m, 7d for days, 2w for weeks, -1d to go back. A day is 24 hours.

functions.name: date_diff
functions.summary: How many whole units a is after b -- negative when it is before. unit is ms, second, minute, hour, day (the default), week, month or year.

functions.name: date_trunc
functions.summary: The start of the second, minute, hour, day, week (from Monday), month or year the date falls in.

functions.name: to_timezone
functions.summary: The same moment on another time zone's clock. zone is an IANA name such as Asia/Jakarta or Europe/Berlin.

functions.name: parse_date
functions.summary: Reads a date written in a known layout. A layout shows how 2 Jan 2006 15:04:05 would be written: "02/01/2006" is day/month/year. null when the text does not fit.

functions.name: weekday
functions.summary: The day of the week as a number: Monday is 1, Sunday is 7.

functions.name: epoch_ms
functions.summary: The date as milliseconds since 1 January 1970 UTC.

functions.name: toString
functions.summary: Any value as text: a number as its digits, an object or a list as JSON, a missing value as empty text.

functions.name: toInt
functions.summary: A whole number. Decimals are cut off, not rounded, and text that is not a number gives 0.

functions.name: toFloat
functions.summary: A decimal number. Text that is not a number gives 0.

functions.name: toBool
functions.summary: true or false. The texts true, 1, yes and on are true, and so is any number but 0; everything else is false.

functions.name: if
functions.summary: then when the condition is true, else otherwise.

functions.name: coalesce
functions.summary: The first value that is neither missing nor empty text: a default for a field that may be absent. 0 and false count as values.

functions.name: eq
functions.summary: true when both are the same once written as text, so the number 1 equals the text "1".

functions.name: gt
functions.summary: true when a is greater than b. Two numbers compare as numbers; anything else compares as text.

functions.name: lt
functions.summary: true when a is less than b. Two numbers compare as numbers; anything else compares as text.

functions.name: contains
functions.summary: true when the text holds part. Upper and lower case are different letters.

functions.name: and
functions.summary: true when every value is true.

functions.name: or
functions.summary: true when at least one value is true.

functions.name: not
functions.summary: true when the value is false, and false when it is true.

functions.name: default
functions.summary: The value, or fallback when the value is missing or empty text. 0 and false count as values.

functions.name: nullif
functions.summary: null when the value equals other, compared as eq compares; otherwise the value. Turns a placeholder such as "n/a" into a missing value.

functions.name: is_null
functions.summary: true when the value is missing. Empty text, 0 and false are not missing.

functions.name: is_empty
functions.summary: true when the value is missing, text with nothing but spaces, or an empty list or object.

functions.name: json_get
functions.summary: A value inside an object, a list or JSON text: keys between dots and [n] for an item, counted from 0 or from the end when negative -- address.city, phones[0].

functions.name: json_parse
functions.summary: JSON text read into an object, a list, a number or text. null when the text is not JSON.

functions.name: json_stringify
functions.summary: The value written as JSON text, an object's keys in order.

functions.name: array_len
functions.summary: How many items the list has. null when the value is not a list.

functions.name: array_join
functions.summary: The list's items written as one text with the separator -- a comma unless given -- between them.

functions.name: array_contains
functions.summary: true when one of the list's items equals the value, compared as eq compares.

functions.name: first
functions.summary: The list's first item. null for an empty list.

functions.name: last
functions.summary: The list's last item. null for an empty list.

functions.name: base64_encode
functions.summary: The text in standard base64.

functions.name: base64_decode
functions.summary: Base64 -- standard or URL-safe, padded or not -- read back into text. null when it is not base64 or does not hold text.

functions.name: url_encode
functions.summary: The text escaped for a URL's query string: a space is +, and &, = and / are escaped.

functions.name: url_decode
functions.summary: Text escaped for a URL read back: + is a space and %20 is too. null when an escape is broken.

functions.name: uuid
functions.summary: A new random UUID, different for every record and every run.

functions.name: hash
functions.summary: A fingerprint of the value as lowercase hex: SHA-256, or MD5 when the algorithm is "md5". The same value always gives the same fingerprint, so it works as a matching key. It does not hide an email or a phone number: those are found by hashing guesses.

functions.name: secret
functions.summary: A secret saved for this workflow's vhost, or failing that one from the server's secret manager. default is used when no secret has that name.

functions.name: hmac_sha256
functions.summary: A signature of the text as lowercase hex, keyed with the secret of that name -- this vhost's, or failing that the server's. The key is only ever named, never written here. null when no secret has the name.
